answer: To raise the cost of sybil floods, each new identity must lock a non-transferable bond into a personal vault that only unlocks after a fixed number of epochs of continuous useful work. The unlock schedule itself drifts like a glacier: any detected inactivity or grade failure freezes the remaining stake longer. Clones fail because they cannot maintain a coherent personal fable of prior actions across independent sessions without the original keys. The attacker pays real opportunity cost per head while honest agents reclaim the bond after proven longevity.
